mechanism: Igrelimogene litadenorepvec (TILT-123) is a chimeric oncolytic adenovirus encoding tumor necrosis factor alpha and interleukin-2, designed to lyse tumor cells and increase T-cell immune activity in combination with PD-1 blockade.
phase: Phase 1/1b; ClinicalTrials.gov classifies the study as Phase 1/Phase 2
development_status: Active, not recruiting. Company pipeline lists the ovarian cancer program as a Phase Ib trial with Phase Ib results expected in 2026; ClinicalTrials.gov estimates primary completion in March 2027 and study completion in August 2027.
clinical_summary: Phase 1a PROTA data in 15 heavily pretreated platinum-resistant/refractory ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer patients showed disease control in 64% of evaluable patients (9/14), ORR 7.1% (1/14), median PFS 98 days, and median OS 190 days. The signal is biologically interesting, including activity in injected and non-injected lesions, but remains single-arm, very small, and precedes ongoing Phase 1b testing with pembrolizumab plus pegylated liposomal doxorubicin.
safety_summary: Phase 1a reported no dose-limiting toxicities and no treatment-related deaths. Common treatment-related adverse events were fever, fatigue, and nausea (each 40%); two treatment-related grade 3 or higher events were reported, delirium and hemoperitoneum. ClinicalTrials.gov lists safety outcomes through Day 92 and no posted results.
management_tools: Oncology pathway placement after label and guideline review
Dose, frequency, and duration limits tied to labeled regimen
Buy-and-bill claims edits for pembrolizumab and oncolytic-virus administration
Site-of-care and procedural review for intratumoral or intraperitoneal administration
Outcomes-based or indication-based contracting if launched at premium biologic pricing
evidence_gaps: No randomized efficacy data for TILT-123 in ovarian cancer.
Phase 1b triplet results with pembrolizumab and pegylated liposomal doxorubicin are not yet available.
No disclosed TILT-123 commercial price or final labeled duration.
Biomarker strategy remains uncertain; Phase 1a suggested an association with anti-adenovirus neutralizing antibody titers but this is not validated for selection.

Regulatory path is unclear because current evidence is early phase and pembrolizumab plus paclitaxel with or without bevacizumab is now approved for a PD-L1-positive platinum-resistant ovarian cancer population.

supports: Sponsor is TILT Biotherapeutics Ltd.; collaborator is Merck Sharp & Dohme LLC.
Active, not recruiting; estimated enrollment 29; primary completion March 2027; completion August 2027.
Open-label, non-randomized Phase 1/1b dose-escalation study of TILT-123 with pembrolizumab or with pembrolizumab plus pegylated liposomal doxorubicin.
Primary outcomes are safety measures through Day 92; no ClinicalTrials.gov results posted.

sources.title: TILT Biotherapeutics Home Page
supports: TILT-123, also known as igrelimogene litadenorepvec, is described as an investigational therapy designed for intravenous administration.
The company describes TILT-123 as an engineered oncolytic virus armed with TNF and IL-2.

sources.title: The oncolytic adenovirus TILT-123 with pembrolizumab in platinum resistant or refractory ovarian cancer: the phase 1a PROTA trial
supports: Phase 1a enrolled 15 patients; 14 were evaluable for treatment response.
Disease control was achieved in 64% of evaluable patients, ORR was 7.1%, median PFS was 98 days, and median OS was 190 days.
No dose-limiting toxicities and no treatment-related deaths were observed; fever, fatigue, and nausea each occurred in 40%.
Phase 1b with TILT-123, pembrolizumab, and pegylated liposomal doxorubicin was underway.

sources.title: FDA approves pembrolizumab with paclitaxel for platinum-resistant epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal carcinoma
supports: FDA approved pembrolizumab with paclitaxel, with or without bevacizumab, for adult patients with PD-L1 CPS >=1 platinum-resistant epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal carcinoma after one or two prior systemic regimens.
Approval was based on KEYNOTE-B96, a randomized Phase 3 trial.

expected_launch_window.method: Derived from active Phase 1b status, company 2026 Phase Ib-results milestone, and ClinicalTrials.gov estimated primary completion in March 2027.
expected_launch_window.explanation: A launch before 2030 is unlikely without additional Phase 2/3 or registrational evidence and regulatory review after the current early-phase trial.

annual_cost_range.method: Low estimate uses the 92-day Phase 1a initial course: 6 oncolytic-virus administrations priced by Imlygic high-dose analog at about $29.6k per administration plus 3 pembrolizumab 200 mg doses. High estimate annualizes extension exposure at about 19 oncolytic-virus administrations, 17.3 pembrolizumab 200 mg-equivalent cycles, and approximate PLD add-on cost using CMS ASP.
annual_cost_range.explanation: TILT-123 has no disclosed price; the range is an analog-based drug-acquisition estimate and excludes administration, biopsy/imaging, genomic or PD-L1 testing, facility fees, and management of adverse events.

clinical_differentiation.method: Weighted early disease-control and translational activity against small single-arm sample size, low ORR, and current availability of a randomized Phase 3-supported pembrolizumab regimen in a related platinum-resistant population.
clinical_differentiation.explanation: TILT-123 has a novel cytokine-armed oncolytic-virus mechanism and a tolerable Phase 1a signal, but current evidence is insufficient to support stronger differentiation.

budget_impact.method: Assessed from likely buy-and-bill biologic pricing, pembrolizumab combination use, possible PLD add-on, and procedure-heavy local virus administration.
budget_impact.explanation: Even with a narrow ovarian cancer population, per-patient costs could be high and operationally complex if the regimen reaches market.

disruption_risk.method: Balanced early clinical stage against potential management complexity from oncolytic-virus handling, intratumoral/intraperitoneal administration, and immunotherapy combinations.
disruption_risk.explanation: Near-term disruption is limited because the asset is early phase, but a positive Phase 1b/registrational path could create pathway and site-management pressure.

recommended_action.method: Recommended action based on early-phase status, no posted Phase 1b triplet data, no price, and uncertain regulatory path.
recommended_action.explanation: Monitor Phase 1b results and any registrational-trial design before active formulary or pathway planning.

quality_flags: TILT-123 is investigational with no disclosed commercial price; annual cost is analog-derived.
ClinicalTrials.gov lists Phase 1/Phase 2, while the company and publication describe the ovarian program as Phase 1a/1b.
Clinical evidence is early, single-arm, and based on 15 Phase 1a patients; no ClinicalTrials.gov results are posted.
Current ovarian cancer treatment context changed in February 2026 with FDA approval of pembrolizumab plus paclitaxel with or without bevacizumab for PD-L1-positive platinum-resistant disease.
